newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian lawman brands president corrupt monster.
newsitem.headline: Colombian lawman brands president corrupt monster.

text.p: A senior government official on Monday criticised one of Colombia's top law enforcers for branding scandal-plagued President Ernesto Samper a "monster of immorality and corruption."

"The only monster threatening Colombian society today is that of immorality and corruption as embodied by the president and many of his aides," Deputy Chief Prosecutor Adolfo Salamanca, one of Samper's fiercest critics within official circles, told El Espectador newspaper on Monday.

His comments sparked an angry response from the president's right-hand man, Interior Minister Horacio Serpa, one of several serving and former ministers under investigation for the role they played in allegedly concealing drug money in Samper's 1994 election campaign.

"(Salamanca's) statements are out of order and are so unnecessarily aggressive that they have lost all objectivity. When such things go beyond the bounds of reason it is not worth responding," Serpa told reporters after an official engagement in Ibague, in central Tolima province.
Salamanca launched his broadside at Samper following the president's suggestions that the national police should no longer be subject to scrutiny by a civilian commissioner.

The deputy prosecutor is a former commissioner and rejects the president's proposal, aired at a summit of police chiefs at the weekend, that the police, part of the armed forces, should be allowed to control, supervise and regulate itself.
In comments to the daily El Espectador, Salamanca said the commissioner's role had helped clean up the police force, root out corruption and restore some of its credibility.
The plan to eliminate the post of commissioner has found favour with National Police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano.
Serpa, a powerful speaker, has taken on the role of defending Samper, often by quoting lines from popular songs to ridicule critics and strike a chord with the public.
